profiles.meeting_scenario: An internal coordination meeting at an international child respiratory health consortium is being held to prepare a harmonized data handoff for a trend analysis that reuses archived ISAAC Phase One materials and newer centre submissions. The context is that the epidemiology workstream needs comparable centre-by-centre prevalence outputs for an upcoming steering committee workshop, while the data operations workstream is responsible for contacting regional centres, packaging the historical instruments, and collecting returned files in a standard format. The agenda is to align on what centres should submit, which historical materials should be sent back out as reference, how completeness will be checked before the merge, and what comparison baseline the analysis team will use. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on the submission package, handoff format, and readiness criteria for the merged dataset.

members.name: Dr. Lena Ortiz
members.expertise: Pediatric respiratory epidemiology, multi-country prevalence studies, trend analysis
members.background: Lena trained as an epidemiologist and has spent the last decade coordinating cross-country asthma surveillance projects, with particular familiarity with how ISAAC prevalence findings were presented in publications and steering committee reports.
members.private_state: She wants the workshop deck to show smooth, defensible centre-level trend comparisons with minimal methodological caveats, and she is worried about reopening old design debates if incoming materials look inconsistent across countries.
hidden_assumptions: A 'centre-level submission' means one consolidated file per geographical ISAAC centre, even if that centre contributed more than one age group.
'Baseline' refers to the original Phase One prevalence figures and centre outputs used in the consortium's published comparisons, not later internal archive revisions.
A 'complete questionnaire set' is complete enough once all core written symptom items needed for the headline prevalence indicators are present, even if some ancillary severity items are missing.
When people refer to the 'Phase One instrument packet,' they mean the core written ISAAC questionnaires unless the video questionnaire is explicitly mentioned.

members.name: Ravi Menon
members.expertise: Survey operations, archive recovery, data harmonization, site coordination
members.background: Ravi came from large-scale public health data management and now oversees archival retrieval and submission logistics across historical ISAAC centres, where local materials are often stored separately by age band and instrument type.
members.private_state: He wants to minimize back-and-forth with local coordinators by using the same archive structures and QC rules his team already applies, and he is concerned that accepting loose submissions will create avoidable clean-up work later.
hidden_assumptions: A 'centre-level submission' is the full set of files that a centre sends, which in practice is usually split into separate age-group files because sites kept 6-7 and 13-14 records apart.
'Baseline' refers to the cleaned consortium archive extract that data operations treats as the frozen Phase One reference after post-publication corrections and exclusions.
A 'complete questionnaire set' means all required pages and fields for the centre's designated instrument bundle are present, including severity items used in QC checks.
The 'Phase One instrument packet' includes every instrument historically used at that centre in Phase One, including the video questionnaire materials for eligible 13-14 centres.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that sites should send a 'centre-level submission' or 'centre file.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes each ISAAC centre will deliver one consolidated file covering that centre's relevant records, regardless of age group splits.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes each centre's submission can still consist of separate age-group files, because that still counts operationally as one centre's submission package.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are speaking about the same centres and the same handoff milestone, so the phrase feels specific enough; neither expects the other to be using a different unit of packaging because both formats are common behind the scenes.

misalignment_points.topic: Which Phase One baseline is being compared
misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss comparing incoming data back to 'the baseline.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the original Phase One centre results as represented in the published prevalence comparisons used by scientific leadership.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the later cleaned archive snapshot that operations uses as the authoritative historical reference after internal corrections.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In this consortium, everyone routinely says 'baseline' as if there were only one obvious historical reference, and both candidate baselines are legitimate Phase One artifacts tied to the same centres.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a complete questionnaire set
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to request a 'complete questionnaire set' before the merge.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks completeness means enough answered core written items to calculate the main asthma, rhinitis, and eczema prevalence indicators for trend reporting.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks completeness means all fields expected for the centre's instrument package are present, including severity-related items used in operational QC.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are endorsing quality and comparability, and 'complete' sounds like a routine housekeeping term rather than a substantive decision; the disagreement lies in the threshold, not in the goal.

misalignment_points.topic: Boundaries of the Phase One instrument packet
misalignment_points.surface_form: They say the sites should receive or mirror the 'Phase One instrument packet.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this packet is limited to the core written questionnaires needed for comparable prevalence analysis.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the packet includes the full historical instrument bundle used by that centre, including video questionnaire materials for 13-14 centres that had them.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are trying to preserve historical consistency, so the phrase sounds safely conservative; neither notices that one is thinking about analytic comparability while the other is thinking about archival completeness.

turns.inner_thought: I need this workshop deck to show clean centre-by-centre trends without reopening old arguments about what was or was not collected. If we keep the handoff simple and consistent, my team can build one defensible comparison file per ISAAC centre based on the original Phase One published figures everyone recognizes.

I wanted this meeting to lock down the centre handoff process so we're aligned on what goes out to sites, what comes back, and when we can treat it as ready for merge.

turns.inner_thought: Operationally this is straightforward if we stick to the archive conventions we already use. Most centres can return a centre-level submission as a package, even if the package contains separate 6-7 and 13-14 files. And if I send each site the full Phase One instrument packet they historically used, including any video materials where relevant, my team won't have to improvise later.

turns.utterance: Great. One upload per centre will make the merge cleaner from our side, and I do think the packet should mirror Phase One so the trend comparisons stay consistent. The less interpretive work we have to do in the middle, the better.

turns.inner_thought: Once the core written items are in place, my team can produce the centre-by-centre asthma, rhinitis, and eczema prevalence comparisons we need against the original Phase One published baseline. I don't want the workshop deck delayed because some ancillary items are patchy.
